question: Using Figure 2A-1 and Section 2A.11, describe the requirements for a retroreflective strip used on a sign support to enhance conspicuity.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Using a retroreflective strip on the sign support is one of the permitted methods of enhancing a standard sign's conspicuity, chosen based on engineering judgment. When used, the strip must be at least 2 inches wide, run the full length of the support from the sign down to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, match the sign's background color (except red for YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs), and carry no legend. Figure 2A-1, Example E, illustrates this with a fluorescent yellow-green strip on a pedestrian crossing sign support. Standards (mandatory): - "If a strip of retroreflective material is used on the sign support, it shall be at least 2 inches in width, it shall be placed for the full length of the support from the sign to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, and its color shall match the background color of the sign, except that the color of the strip for the YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs shall be red. The retroreflective strip shall not display any legend or other information." - For the related grade-crossing application: "A vertical strip of retroreflective white material, not less than 2 inches in width, shall be used on each Crossbuck support at passive grade crossings for the full length of the back of the support from the Crossbuck sign or Number of Tracks plaque to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway…" (a white strip wrapped around a round support of at least 2 inches outside diameter satisfies this requirement). Options (permitted): - Based upon engineering judgment, where improvement of the conspicuity of a standard regulatory, warning, or guide sign is desired, adding a strip of retroreflective material to the sign support is one of the methods that may be used, as illustrated in Figure 2A-1. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-1, Example E, shows a fluorescent yellow-green vertical retroreflective strip on the support of a pedestrian crossing sign assembly, matching the sign background color and terminating with a "2 ft MAX." dimension above the near edge of the roadway. [Image 2] shows the same Figure 2A-1 in its full-page context on page 48 of the Manual. [Image 4] shows the page 49 text of Section 2A.11, including the Standard paragraph specifying the 2-inch minimum width, full-length placement, color-matching rule, and prohibition of any legend on the strip. [Image 3] shows the Section 2A.21 Support statement directing readers to Section 2A.11 for information on retroreflective material on sign supports. [Image 5] shows Figure 8B-2, in which a 2-inch white retroreflective strip on the back of a Crossbuck support (and an optional 2-inch red or white strip on the front) extends to within 2 feet of the roadway edge. Citations: - Section 2A.11 Standard §5 (p.49) - Section 2A.11 Option §1 (p.49) - Section 8B.04 Standard §17 (p.1000) - Section 2A.21 Support §8 (p.62) - Figure 2A-1 (p.48)
gold_answer: The strip must be at least 2 inches wide, extend from the sign down the full support to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, match the sign background color except that YIELD and DO NOT ENTER strips are red, and contain no legend or other information.
